source_text:
φανῇ, πρὶν οἱ Μάγοι παραγένωνται, μή ποτε ὑβρισθῶ μεν. Τὸ γὰρ ἐξ ἐμοῦ φῶς
1
προλαβεῖν χρὴ τοῦ ἀστέρος τὴν εἰς Βηθλεὲμ ἄφιξιν, ὥστε γνωσθῆναι ὅτι παρ' ἐμοῦ
καὶ τὸν δρόμον ὁδηγεῖται καὶ τὴν ἀκτῖνα δανείζεται. Ἀλλὰ σὺ μὴ ζημιωθῇς ἂν
ἀκρόβυστοι τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τῆς εὐλογίας θερίσωσιν.»
6 «Καὶ εὐλόγησεν τὸν θεὸν καὶ εἶπεν· νῦν ἀπολύεις τὸν δοῦ λόν σου,
δέσποτα, κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου ἐν εἰρήνῃ.» Εὐλόγησεν τὸν θεὸν τὸν Πατέρα σὺν τῷ Υἱῷ,
τὸν Υἱὸν σὺν τῷ Πνεύματι, ἐπειδὴ τὸ Πνεῦμα μὲν τὸ χρηματίζον ἐτύγχανεν, τὸν Υἱὸν
δὲ μετὰ χεῖρας ἐβάσταζεν, σαρκὶ φανῆναι καὶ βρέφος δι' ἡμᾶς γενέσθαι
εὐδοκήσαντα· ὁ δὲ Πατὴρ καὶ αὐτὸς ἐνεργῶν ἦν τὰ τοσαῦτα καὶ τηλικαῦτα μυστήρια.
Ἀλλὰ τὴν εὐχαριστίαν ἐπὶ τίνι προσέφερεν; «Νῦν», φησίν, «ἀπολύεις τὸν δοῦλόν
σου, δέσποτα», ὅτε μοι φόβος οὐκ ἔστι θανάτου, μετὰ χαρᾶς δὲ πρὸς τοὺς νεκροὺς
τὴν ζωὴν αὐτοῖς καταγγελῶν ἀπέρχομαι. «Ἀπολύεις δὲ κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου ἐν
εἰρήνῃ», ἐκεῖνο ὅπερ ∆αυὶδ ὁ προφήτης παρὰ σοῦ δανεισάμενος ἔλεγεν· «Ἐν εἰρήνῃ
ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ κοιμηθήσομαι καὶ ὑπνώσω.»
7 «Ὅτι εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου τὸ σωτήριόν σου», ὃ πολλοὶ μὲν τῶν
προφητῶν ἐπεθύμησαν ἰδεῖν· νῦν δὲ αὐτῇ τῇ πειρᾷ τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων
παρέστησας τὸν ὕψιστον δι' ἡμᾶς τοσοῦ τον ὥστε βρέφος γενέσθαι ταπεινούμενον·
οὔτε γὰρ ἄλλως σῶσαι τὸν φθαρέντα πηλὸν ὁ κεραμεύς, ἀλλ' αὐτὸς αὐτῷ
συναναφυρεὶς ἔμελλεν. «Εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου τὸ σωτήριόν σου, ὃ ἡτοίμασας κατὰ
πρόσωπον πάντων τῶν λαῶν», ἀλλὰ πάντων, ἐπειδὴ πάντων ὑπ άρχων δημιουργὸς
πᾶσι προέθηκας τὸ τῆς σωτηρίας ἀναγκαίως μυ στήριον. «Φῶς εἰς ἀποκάλυψιν
ἐθνῶν καὶ δόξαν λαοῦ σου Ἰσραήλ»· πρότερον τὰ ἔθνη φωτίζεται καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο
Ἰσραὴλ δοξάζεται· ἐτέχθη γὰρ οὗτος ἐφ' οὗ πρῶτοι μὲν οἱ ἔσχατοι, ἔσχατοι δὲ οἱ
πρῶτοι, τὰ πρεσβεῖα τῶν ἔμπροσθεν διὰ ῥαθυμίαν ζημιωθέντων, γεγόνασιν.
8 «Καὶ ἦν ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ θαυμάζοντες ἐπὶ τοῖς λαλουμένοις περὶ
αὐτοῦ.» Τίνος χάριν πατέρα τὸν Ἰωσήφ, ὦ τῆς θείας γενεαλογίας εὐαγγελιστὰ καὶ
συγγραφεῦ, καλεῖς; Αὐτὸς γὰρ εἰπόντα τὸν Γαβριὴλ πρὸς τὴν παρθένον ἀπέδειξας,
ἡνίκα πῶς ἡ σύλληψις ἔσται καὶ τίνα τρόπον ἡ παρθένος τέξε ται μεθωδεύετο·
«Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ δύναμις ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι.» – «Οὐκ
ἐπιλέλησμαι τῶν ἐμαυτοῦ», φησίν· «εἰ γὰρ καὶ λήθην ἐλάμβανον, τὸ Πνεῦμα ἂν
ἐμίμνησκεν. Ἀλλ' οὕτω τότε καλεῖσθαι τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ὁ σαρκωθεὶς ἐβούλετο, ὅπως
ἀπατηθῇ ὁ ἐνεδρεύων τὸ τῆς σωτηρίας τῆς ἡμετέρας μυστή ριον.» «Ἐθαύμαζον δὲ
ἐπὶ τοῖς λεγομένοις περὶ αὐτοῦ», ἐπειδὴ βρέφος ὁ πρεσβύτης ἐβάσταζεν, θεοῦ δὲ
ὕμνους ἐφθέγγετο. «Καὶ εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς Συμεών»· ἐχρῆν γὰρ εὐλογεῖσθαι τοὺς
τὴν εὐλογίαν τοῖς ὑπὸ κατάραν πράττουσιν διακονήσαντας.
thought_title: The Spirit urges Simeon to seize the blessing before the Magi; Simeon's thanksgiving and the evangelist's defense of calling Joseph father
orientation: Hesychius is expanding the Presentation account, imagining the Holy Spirit's words to Simeon and then explaining Simeon's song and the evangelist's wording.
pass_a_gloss: before the star appears, before the Magi arrive, lest we be insulted. For the light from me must anticipate the arrival of the star at Bethlehem, so that it may be known that from me it is guided in its course and borrows its ray. But may you not suffer loss if the uncircumcised reap the firstfruits of the blessing. And he blessed God and said: now you release your servant, Master, according to your word in peace. He blessed God the Father with the Son, the Son with the Spirit, since the Spirit was the one giving the oracle, and the Son he was carrying in his arms, who was pleased to appear in flesh and become an infant for us; and the Father himself was also working such great and mighty mysteries. But for what was he offering the thanksgiving? Now, he says, you release your servant, Master, when there is no fear of death for me, but with joy I depart to the dead announcing life to them. And you release according to your word in peace, that which David the prophet, having borrowed from you, said: In peace I will lie down and sleep at the same time. Because my eyes have seen your salvation, which many of the prophets desired to see; but now by actual experience you have presented to the race of humans the Most High so greatly humbled for us as to become an infant; for the potter could not otherwise save the ruined clay, but he himself was going to be mixed together with it. My eyes have seen your salvation, which you prepared before the face of all the peoples, but of all, since being the creator of all you set before all necessarily the mystery of salvation. A light for revelation of the nations and glory of your people Israel; first the nations are illumined and after this Israel is glorified; for this one was born for whom the first became last and the last became first, the privileges of those ahead being lost through negligence. And his father and his mother were marveling at the things spoken about him. For what reason do you call Joseph father, O evangelist and writer of the divine genealogy? For you yourself showed Gabriel saying to the virgin, when it was being arranged how the conception would be and in what manner the virgin would give birth: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. I have not forgotten my own words, he says; for even if I were taking forgetfulness, the Spirit would have reminded me. But the Incarnate One willed Joseph to be called father then, so that the one lying in wait against the mystery of our salvation might be deceived. And they were marveling at the things said about him, because the old man was carrying an infant, and was uttering hymns of God. And Simeon blessed them; for it was necessary that those who ministered the blessing to those under a curse be blessed.

choices.why: The Spirit speaks as sharing in the divine work; the passive subjunctive with μή ποτε expresses a feared outcome, not a mild 'disgraced'.
Keeps the literal bodily term, which is the point of the contrast with the firstfruits of blessing.
The participle denotes the Spirit's ongoing oracular activity toward Simeon, not merely 'speaking'.
The compound verb conveys the potter's intimate mingling with the clay, essential to the image.
The participle has an ambush sense, matching the military metaphor of the enemy lurking against the mystery.

pass_b_english: appears, before the Magi arrive, so that we are not insulted. For the light that comes from me must anticipate the star's arrival in Bethlehem, so that it may be known that from me the star both receives guidance for its course and borrows its ray. But do not suffer loss, if the uncircumcised should harvest the firstfruits of the blessing.”

“And he blessed God and said: ‘Now you release your servant, Master, according to your word, in peace’” (Luke 2:28-29). He blessed God the Father together with the Son, and the Son together with the Spirit, because the Spirit was the one giving the oracle, while he held the Son in his arms—the Son who was pleased to appear in flesh and to become an infant for our sake. And the Father himself was also at work in mysteries so great and so mighty.

But for what did he offer thanksgiving? “Now,” he says, “you release your servant, Master,” because now I have no fear of death, but with joy I go to the dead, announcing life to them. “You release me according to your word, in peace”—that word which David the prophet, having borrowed from you, spoke: “In peace I will lie down and sleep” (Psalm 4:8).

“For my eyes have seen your salvation” (Luke 2:30), which many of the prophets desired to see. But now by actual experience you have presented to the human race the Most High, humbled for our sake to such a degree that he became an infant. For the potter could not otherwise save the ruined clay unless he himself was going to be mixed together with it. “My eyes have seen your salvation, which you prepared before the face of all the peoples” (Luke 2:30-31)—all of them, because being the creator of all, you necessarily set before all the mystery of salvation. “A light for revelation to the nations and glory for your people Israel” (Luke 2:32). First the nations are enlightened, and after this Israel is glorified. For this one was born for whom the first became last and the last became first, since those who were ahead lost the privileges of the front ranks through carelessness.

“And his father and his mother were marveling at what was being said about him” (Luke 2:33). Why do you call Joseph the father, O evangelist and writer of the divine genealogy? For you yourself showed that Gabriel spoke to the virgin when he explained how the conception would occur and in what manner the virgin would give birth: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you” (Luke 1:35). “I have not forgotten my own words,” he says. “For even if I were forgetful, the Spirit would remind me. But the Incarnate One willed Joseph to be called father at that time, so that the one lying in wait against the mystery of our salvation might be deceived.” “They were marveling at what was being said about him,” because the old man was holding an infant, yet he was uttering hymns to God. “And Simeon blessed them” (Luke 2:34). For it was fitting that those who ministered the blessing to those under a curse should themselves be blessed.

problems.quote: but with joy I depart to the dead, announcing life to them
problems.source_quote: μετὰ χαρᾶς δὲ πρὸς τοὺς νεκροὺς τὴν ζωὴν αὐτοῖς καταγγελῶν ἀπέρχομαι
problems.why: πρὸς τοὺς νεκροὺς ἀπέρχομαι = 'I go to the dead'; τὴν ζωὴν αὐτοῖς καταγγελῶν = 'announcing life to them'. Word order shows 'to the dead' goes with 'I go', not 'announcing'.
problems.fix: but with joy I go to the dead, announcing life to them

edits.old: but with joy I depart to the dead, announcing life to them
edits.new: but with joy I go to the dead, announcing life to them

fixed: The English 'depart to the dead' is acceptable, but the source word order (πρὸς τοὺς νεκροὺς ἀπέρχομαι) places 'to the dead' with the verb of going, and 'depart' is slightly less precise than 'go'. Changed to 'go' for accuracy.

last_rejected.why: αὐτῇ τῇ πειρᾷ means 'by this trial/test' not 'by actual experience'; the sense is testing not experiential knowledge.
last_rejected.ruling: πειρᾷ here means 'experience' not 'trial'; 'actual experience' captures the sense of firsthand seeing.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'first the nations are enlightened' (πρότερον = first/before), but English 'First' could read as enumeration; the contrast 'before...after' with Israel is the point.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'First' renders πρότερον accurately; temporal contrast with 'after this' is clear.

last_rejected.quote: "I have not forgotten my own words," he says. "For even if I were forgetful, the Spirit would remind me. But the Incarnate One willed Joseph to be called father at that time, so that the one lying in wait against the mystery of our salvation might be deceived."
last_rejected.source_quote: «Οὐκ ἐπιλέλησμαι τῶν ἐμαυτοῦ», φησίν· «εἰ γὰρ καὶ λήθην ἐλάμβανον, τὸ Πνεῦμα ἂν ἐμίμνησκεν. Ἀλλ' οὕτω τότε καλεῖσθαι τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ὁ σαρκωθεὶς ἐβούλετο, ὅπως ἀπατηθῇ ὁ ἐνεδρεύων τὸ τῆς σωτηρίας τῆς ἡμετέρας μυστήριον.»
last_rejected.why: English hides that the evangelist Luke is the imagined speaker defending himself; "he says" makes it ambiguous.
last_rejected.fix: "I have not forgotten my own account," says the evangelist. "For even if I were forgetful, the Spirit would remind me. But the Incarnate One willed Joseph to be called father then, so that the enemy lying in wait against our salvation's mystery might be deceived."
last_rejected.ruling: φησίν is 'he says'; context makes Luke the speaker clear. Not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: the Spirit was the one giving the oracle
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ Πνεῦμα μὲν τὸ χρηματίζον ἐτύγχανεν
last_rejected.why: "Giving the oracle" misrepresents χρηματίζον; the Spirit was the one making the oracular response/prophetic utterance to Simeon.
last_rejected.fix: the Spirit was the one who had spoken the oracle to him
last_rejected.ruling: χρηματίζον means giving oracular response; 'giving the oracle' is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: the one lying in wait against the mystery of our salvation
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁ ἐνεδρεύων τὸ τῆς σωτηρίας τῆς ἡμετέρας μυστήριον
last_rejected.why: "The one lying in wait against" obscures that this is the devil/enemy; ἐνεδρεύων here implies ambush by a hostile agent.
last_rejected.fix: the enemy lurking in ambush against the mystery of our salvation
last_rejected.ruling: ἐνεδρεύων means 'lying in wait'; rendering the literal sense is valid, not a meaning change.
